category_title: Silent English Language Learners with extensive digital literacy practices
minimal_context: Wei is participating in a public discussion forum on the class website to ask questions about a unit on Transcendentalism.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please use this public discussion forum to share your ideas and questions about our unit on Transcendentalism.

STUDENT: hahaha.....!!! no one want to talk here.....!!! just the one that never talk in class.....!!

TUTOR: Remember to post your questions about the reading assignment.

STUDENT: (Posting under the pseudonym 'what a sad boy') i am worried about failing... i literally do not talk in class because i do not know enough english...

TUTOR: Just type your question about the text.

STUDENT: HeY hEy HEy Is Me........!!! me mEEEEeEE mEeEEEEeee ....!! teacher~~~I wAnt tO aSk YoU Is tHiS fReE tHouGht O r s e l f - r E l i A n C e “ i J u S t … W a N t T o l I v E w H i L e i Am aLiVe~~~~ .....!!!!!”

options.A: Invest in getting to know the student over time, communicating with him to ensure he is not treated as a deficient learner lacking the skills to succeed.
options.B: Invite the student to participate in a choral reading of a shared text about Transcendentalism alongside peers during the traditional classroom session.
options.C: Brainstorm aloud variations of the forum posts, use speech recognition to generate transcriptions, and model how to use speech recognition and invented spelling to write drafts on the forum.
options.D: Provide a reflective journal prompt that includes a set of metacognitive prompts (My Analysis, My Motivation, My Problem, My Plan) and prompt sheets with content-related questions about Transcendentalism.
